First, the user asked about the longest win streak in MLB history. The Planner decided to use WebSurfer to gather information. The WebSurfer went to DuckDuckGo and found some initial results, but they were just links and didn't give concrete info. Then the Planner told WebSurfer to check MLB.com and Baseball-Reference.

WebSurfer went to MLB.com, but the page didn't clearly state the all-time record. Then WebSurfer went to Baseball-Reference, which had the schedule for the 1916 Giants. The season summary there showed a 26-game winning streak, but it included a tie, so the actual uninterrupted wins were shorter.

The Planner concluded the longest streak was 26 games, citing Baseball-Reference. But according to the examples, the mistake was in not verifying the exact scope of the streak and not cross-checking with other sources to confirm it was regular-season only and without ties.

So, the error was in the Planner's synthesis of the information, not cross-verifying the streak's nature and scope. The Planner didn't ensure the streak was wins-only and didn't check other authoritative sources to confirm the record.
